messages:
mike: Heads up — we saw another burst of scale thrash in us-west-2 this morning when a model A traffic spike coincided with spot reclaim waves. Autoscaler spun up 12 nodes then immediately drained 6 when interruptions came back. Thinking we should try an adaptive cooldown that factors in recent interruption rate + queue depth.

olivia: Ugh, saw those logs. The reclaim logs show mostly same-AZ preempts. Cost taking a hit because we over-provisioned fast then paid for partial hours. Can you paste the eviction pattern?

mike: Pasted excerpt from node-events:```
NODE i-0ab123: spot-termination-notice at 04:12:03
NODE i-0cd456: spot-healthy -> terminating at 04:13:01
autoscaler: scale_up 12 -> nodes_ready 04:14:40
autoscaler: scale_down 6 -> drain_start 04:15:02
```

devin: Two quick thoughts: (1) Add a short-window interruption-rate metric to gating — if interruption prob > 8% in last 10m, reduce surge target to +30% (instead of +100%). (2) Make scale-out hysteresis proportional to queued inference tokens, not just pod count.

rachel: I like tying to tokens. For inference, backpressure is token-level (requests/sec + avg seq length). We could compute an estimated token backlog = queue.size * avg_seq_len and use that to decide fast vs slow lanes.

andrew: Agree. Also propose a "slow-burn" surge lane: allow a limited number of servers to come up faster (fast path) and put remainder behind a progressive cooldown. Example: target_surge=40%, fast_lane=10% immediate, remaining 30% ramp over 8-12min with exponential backoff.

mike: That would avoid immediate full-fleet churn. How do we detect when to bypass hedging? For planned traffic spikes (deploys/cron) we want deterministic behavior.

olivia: Use signals: (a) traffic spike with request origin tag = rollout, (b) manual annotation in rollout job, (c) scheduled window. If annotated, set aggressive scale policy ignore-interruption for X minutes. We already support rollout headers in the API.

kai: Concern: ignoring interruptions temporarily risks tails for other customers in same AZ. Suggest we keep cost cap guardrail: if preemptible loss > Y tokens or we exceed per-tenant egress, abort aggressive mode.

devin: Implementation sketch: 1) new metric "spot_interrupt_rate_10m" from node-exporter; 2) token_backlog estimate pipeline (ingest request/sec + seq_len) into prometheus; 3) autoscaler policy: if interrupt_rate < 5% and token_backlog > threshold -> fast path; if interrupt_rate 5-15% -> slow-burn; if >15% -> conservative (no new spot until hedged). Include cooldown windows: adaptive_cooldown = base_cooldown * (1 + interrupt_rate).

mike: Experiment plan: rollout in staging first for 2 weeks, then us-west-2 canary (10% traffic), monitor: scale events/min, avg node hour wasted (partial-hour nodes), tail latency 99.9, token loss due to preempts.

rachel: I'll add an eval set focused on short-burst tail latencies. Also add a synthetic spike job at 03:00 UTC to simulate morning traffic.

andrew: Ops runbook notes: if thrash resumes, we can flip `autoscaler.feature.adaptive_cooldown=false` via feature flag. Also add alert: "excessive_partial_hours" when < 30% nodes run > 45m but < 60m.

sre-bot: deploybot: feature flag created: autoscaler.adaptive_cooldown (owner: mike). Scheduled rollout window: staging 48h.

mike: I'll draft a PR for the policy code and a k8s config with example thresholds. PR will include graphs and the schedule. Thanks all — let's sync tomorrow 11:00 PST to lock thresholds. :thumbsup:
__notes: Each message line is a chronological entry in the thread. No title field per agents.md.
